title: GPU Node Allocator + Autoscale Bridge (Terraform) for Private VPC
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (terraform-gpu-node-allocator) that provisions GPU node groups inside customer Private VPCs and provides a pluggable autoscaling bridge supporting both ASG-based scaling and Karpenter-based scaling. The module must: 1) integrate with Private control plane networking and enforce subnet/endpoint constraints; 2) expose health-check probes and graceful drain policies for runtime upgrades; 3) provide safe default taints/labels for mixed instance/accelerator fleets; 4) include an upgrade-safe lifecycle and canary hooks to avoid mass eviction during kernel/driver upgrades. This ticket covers spec, implementation, tests, docs, and a pilot rollout to one internal customer instance.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module can create GPU node groups in Private VPC with variables for instance family, AMI, and accelerator type
Module provides a toggle to select autoscaler mode: "asg" or "karpenter" and wires up the appropriate IAM roles and nodeClass/nodeTemplate where applicable
Upgrade lifecycle supports staged driver upgrades with configurable batch size and node draining hooks
Health checks: node kubelet readiness + custom agent heartbeat metric exposed to CloudWatch/Prometheus for 1-minute flaky detection
Canary rollout workflow exists (terraform flag + smoke test) and a documented rollback path
E2E test harness (local/integration) validates node creation, scale up/down, and a simulated driver upgrade without application SLO violations
Module is published to internal registry with versioned docs and an example usage in private-deploy/examples/gpu-fleet.tf
tasks: Draft module API and variables; include security-sensitive defaults (SSH disabled, restricted SGs)
Implement ASG path: launch template composition, lifecycle hooks, health checks integration
Implement Karpenter path: nodeClass/nodeTemplate generation and taint/label conventions
Add upgrade orchestration: pre-drain hooks, grace period defaults, post-upgrade health gating
Build e2e integration tests using our internal terraform-test harness
Add docs, examples, and migration guide for customers using legacy GPU modules
Run pilot with internal customer staging environment and collect telemetry
implementation_notes: Prefer reusable helper modules (launch-template, iam-role, node-annotations) to avoid copy/paste
Use provider version pinning in examples and validate with 'terraform validate' + 'tflint' in CI
Expose variables for driver-install hooks; default to our curated driver bootstrap but allow custom script_url
Karpenter path will create nodeTemplate with accelerators as extended resources (resourceRequests) and a taint to prefer GPU workloads
ASG path will use instance metadata tags to signal readiness to the control plane health checker
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind feature-flagged module registry entry (v0.1.0-beta)
Deploy to internal staging Private VPC and run smoke tests (scale 0->3, run synthetic SLOs)
Enable canary on 10% of traffic/customers for 48 hours with automated rollback on health regression
Promote to GA after 2 successful canaries and security review sign-off
test_plan: Unit tests for Terraform module using terratest for resource attribute assertions
Integration: spin up minimal Private VPC in CI, provision module with ASG and Karpenter modes, run workload that exercises KV cache and sustained token generation
Upgrade test: simulate driver AMI bump and run staged drains; assert <2% request error increase
Chaos test: kill random GPU nodes during rollout to validate autoscaler and fallback behavior
risks: Driver upgrades on heterogeneous fleets could trigger simultaneous reboots if draining is misconfigured
Karpenter vs ASG semantics differ; misconfiguring taints/labels could lead to incorrect scheduling and cost blowup
IAMscoping mistakes may expose node roles beyond intended VPC boundaries
E2E tests in CI are flaky due to cloud quota limits — plan for a dedicated test account
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose node heartbeats as metric: gpu_node_heartbeat{env="$env"} and set alert if <90% nodes report in 2 minutes
Auto page on scale-failure (ASG instance launch failures or Karpenter provisioning timeouts) with runbook link
Dashboard: per-cluster GPU utilization, node age distribution, pending pod counts, and driver upgrade progress
A nightly job will run smoke prompts across a representative workload and report regression deltas to the Optimize pipeline
